cases.reason: A benefit/cost explanation of persistent structures is achievable using supplied versions and shared-substructure diagrams. It need not first implement an OO list.
cases.completeAdmissibleAcquisitionExample: Compare immutable [1,2] with a new [1,2,3] version: copying all elements versus sharing unchanged parts explains old-version retention and storage/copy costs. The goal supplies the new representation.
cases.scopeLimit: No imperative implementation or OO class is asserted by the whole DE/EN goal; the broader ancestor name is not itself a compulsory implementation gate.

cases.reason: Mapping stack/queue operations onto a supplied list is the full target performance. c62 additionally requires developing AND implementing general algorithms, which is not necessary for this mapping performance.
cases.completeAdmissibleAcquisitionExample: Given [Anna,Ben], push(Cara),pop yields Cara then [Anna,Ben]; enqueue(Cara),dequeue yields Anna then [Ben,Cara]. A table of operations and resulting lists fulfills the target without writing a list-processing program.
cases.scopeLimit: Replace with orientation only. LIFO/FIFO and their representation on a given list belong to acquisition of this goal; no new code or target text is needed.

cases.reason: The target explicitly develops recursive insertion/deletion/traversal for a GIVEN singly linked list MODEL. Structuring recursion with termination and parameters is a precise method prerequisite. The existing full OO design goal is broader.
cases.completeAdmissibleAcquisitionExample: Use empty or Node(value,rest) and a supplied head/rest interface. Recursive traversal has a base case and recursive rest call; insertion/deletion can be developed on this given model without first designing an OO class.
cases.scopeLimit: This does not waive the learner's own recursive algorithm development; only the unnecessary representation-specific preparation is removed.

cases.scopeLimit: No prerequisite to recursion or OO representation is invented; parent context has no authored universal OO requirement.

cases.reason: For the conventional binary heap as the stated first acquisition model, binary-tree structure and node operations are directly relevant: complete shape, parent/child relations and sift operations build on them. An OO linked list is not required.
cases.completeAdmissibleAcquisitionExample: Represent a complete binary heap by an array, parent floor((i-1)/2), children2i+1 and2i+2; insertion/extraction move values along this tree. This demonstrates the new foundation without OO-list implementation.
cases.scopeLimit: The original goal does not require every heap variant. This review accepts the explicit conventional binary-heap first model already documented by the proposal; it does not introduce a claim that arbitrary nonbinary heap families require binary-tree mastery.

cases.reason: LRU/LFU implementation/evaluation needs algorithms over stored entries, which an existing array/list algorithm competence supplies. The target does not require O(1) operations or an OO-list class.

cases.scopeLimit: This retains actual algorithm development/implementation preparation; only one unnecessary concrete data-structure design is removed.

cases.reason: Simple declarative graph algorithms need graph nodes/edges/paths plus the retained Prolog-list operations. Adding graph vocabulary is a precise direct foundation after removal of whole-exam routes.

cases.reason: The complete target is DB connection, preparing SQL and outputting a result set. The added fd1 prerequisite also demands independently formulating JOIN and sorting. No bound source/task context was found requiring those extra performances beforehand.

Variables/I-O are used; neither JOIN nor ORDER BY is formulated. This is a complete admissible integration acquisition example.
cases.scopeLimit: Replace value with only18317. SQL integration/placeholder use is acquired in0cfb; this does not assert general SELECT mastery or implicit completion of fd1.
